commits.message:
docs(readme): document the package subpaths and the mobx install (rich-packaging-1xv.6)

Every import the README showed came from the bare package name, so a reader
following it wrote `import { Button } from "@promptctl/rich-js"` and got
nothing — widgets left the main barrel two commits ago. Finding the right
subpath did not save them either: mobx is a peer marked optional, so
`npm install @promptctl/rich-js` does not fetch it and does not warn, and
`@promptctl/rich-js/widgets` fails at import with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND until
they install it themselves.

An "Entry points" table under Installing now names the four areas that live
behind a subpath and why each does — `./widgets` and `./template-bindings`
for a third-party runtime dependency of their own, `./host` for the terminal
seam, `./node/*` because they read node built-ins and the main entry point
stays browser-safe. The table has no "what you must install" column, because
the two dependency-carrying subpaths are not symmetric: mobx is the
consumer's to install, while `@promptctl/go-template-js` is a plain
dependency that arrives with the package. That asymmetry is carried in prose
so it cannot be flattened into a row shape.

A new Interactive Widgets section adds the first snippet that constructs a
widget, adapted from docs/widgets.md and kept complete enough to run — the
Ctrl+C handler included, since raw mode traps a reader who copies a shorter
version. The Status snippet imported only `Console` while calling
`new Status(...)`; `Status` is on the barrel, so the import now names it.

Nothing in the test suite reads README.md, so the snippets were checked by
hand: every module specifier resolved through node's own resolver against
`package.json#exports`, and the widget snippet type-checked under `strict`
against the built declarations.

perf(packaging)!: make mobx an optional peer (rich-packaging-1xv.5) (#121)

mobx was a hard runtime dependency, so every consumer installed it whether
or not a widget was ever constructed. The widgets split already took it out
of the default bundle; this takes it out of the default install.

It is now a peer dependency marked optional in peerDependenciesMeta, which
is the only spelling that does what the ticket asked. optionalDependencies
would not have: npm installs those and merely tolerates a build failure. A
bare peer would not have either, since npm 7+ auto-installs peers. The pair
is what makes npm neither fetch mobx nor warn about its absence. It stays in
devDependencies so this checkout's tests and demos still run.

Measured by packing a tarball and installing it into an empty project:
8 packages before, 7 after, no mobx and no peer warning. The barrel renders
a Table with mobx absent; @promptctl/rich-js/widgets fails at import with
ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND until mobx is installed, and constructs a Button once
it is. All 10 demo bundles still boot in Chromium under playwright.

BREAKING CHANGE: consumers of @promptctl/rich-js/widgets must now install
mobx themselves — `npm install @promptctl/rich-js mobx`.

The hazard this creates is invisible here by construction, which is why it
comes with a gate. mobx stays in devDependencies, so an `import { observable }
from "mobx"` added under src/core/ would type-check, pass every test, run
every demo and build the docs — then break every downstream consumer at
install time. test/seam/optional-peers.test.ts walks the runtime import graph
from each package.json#exports entry separately and reports three ways: a
package declared nowhere, an optional peer reached from an entry that does
not provide it, and a PEER_PROVIDERS entry that can no longer reach the
package. Confirmed red by staging that exact import into src/core/measure.ts;
it named the file, the line and the chain.

classifySpecifier moves to test/seam/specifiers.ts, which browser-safe.ts now
shares rather than keeping a private copy — the same reason identifiers.ts
exists. test/coverage/extract.ts gains PACKAGE_MANIFEST, one parse of
package.json, and deliberately does not model devDependencies: a rule that
consulted it would call a dependency satisfied because we happen to have it.

@promptctl/go-template-js is the same shape and was left alone on purpose;
it is filed as rich-packaging-1xv.dpo to be decided on its own merits.
